title: The effect on emotions and brain activity by the direct/indirect lighting in the residential environment

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight)
findings.mechanism: The participants felt more pleasant in the direct/indirect lighting environment, indicating that space with direct/indirect lighting modulated subjective perception.
findings.quote: The valence ratings for direct/indirect lighting (mean = 6.4, SD = 1.2) were significantly higher (P=0.005)

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment vs. direct lighting environment
findings.mechanism: arousal was modulated by brightness [31,32] or color temperature [16]. The lighting conditions only differed in the ratio of direct and indirect light - illuminance and color temperature were constant.
findings.quote: arousal did not significantly differ between both conditions.

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight)
findings.mechanism: The participants felt cooler...in the direct/indirect lighting environment...This result is in line with those of our previous behavioral study [39].
findings.quote: The cool scores for direct/indirect lighting...were significantly higher (P=0.045) than those for direct lighting

stimuli.description: A furnished living room (4.7m x 4.4m x 3.1m) with eight LED lighting panels. Two conditions: 1) direct/indirect lighting (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) and 2) direct lighting (700 lx downlight). Illuminance was controlled at 700 lx and color temperature at 5000K for both conditions.
stimuli.source: Environmental setting and Design and procedure sections, Figure 1

tables.description: Within-group subjective parameter comparisons between direct/indirect and direct lighting conditions.

limitations: Subjective feelings toward the environment can be altered depending on the amount of sunshine, lighting hardware, length of suspended lighting, interior decoration, and other variables.
The study did not employ multiple comparisons due to its explorative nature, raising the possibility of detecting a type 1 error.
Participants may have assumed the hypothesis, potentially influencing results, despite being uninformed about it.
The sample size (28) is small for the generalization of results, although sufficient for EEG activity investigation.
